exam.subject: Chemistry
exam.title: ESSCE-style Chemistry Model Exam 2016/2017

parts.title: Part I – Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: Part I contains 75 questions. You must answer all of them. Each question carries 1 point. Write all answers on the SCANTRON GENERAL PURPOSE ANSWER SHEET. There is only one best answer for each question.

parts.title: Part II – Work Out and/or Essay Type Questions
parts.instructions: Part II contains work out and/or essay type questions. You must answer all of them. This part carries twenty-five points. Write your answers on the separate answer sheet provided.

source.prepared_by: Chemistry Department, Warsay Yikealo Secondary School Sawa, Feb. 2017
source.note: Extracted from the 2016/2017 Sawa model-exam Word file. Cover says Part II has six questions; the paper prints seven numbered items that sum to 25 points. Notation 168O 2- treated as ¹⁶₈O²⁻. No official key.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key exists. All answers were solved independently and checked against the Eritrean MoE Chemistry textbooks Grades 9–12.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents a physical change?
explanation_steps: Rule: a physical change does not make a new substance.
Working: corrosion, fermentation and burning make new substances. Salt dissolving is still NaCl + water.
tips: Chemical change = new substance. Dissolving is physical.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – Chemistry: The Study of Matter

questions.stem: The number of protons, electrons and neutrons for the atom ¹⁶₈O²⁻ are respectively
explanation_steps: Rule: Z = protons = 8; neutrons = A−Z = 8; electrons = Z+2 = 10 for the 2− ion.
tips: Anions have more electrons than protons.

A neutral ¹²₆C atom has electrons

questions.stem: Which of the following sets of atoms / ions are iso-electronic to each other? (At. No. Na=11, Ne=10, Li=3, He=2, Mg=12, Ca=20)
explanation_steps: Given: look for the same electron count.
Rule: Na⁺ has 10 e; Ne has 10 e.
Working: Ca²⁺ has 18 e, not 10. Li⁺ has 2 e.
tips: Isoelectronic = same number of electrons.

questions.stem: A liquid has no fixed shape but it takes the shape of its container in which it is placed. This is b/ce

options.A: The particles are not in a fixed position.
options.B: The particles have the lowest amount of energy.
options.C: The particles have slight attraction for one another.
options.D: The particles can vibrate in their fixed positions.

explanation_steps: Rule: liquid particles move (not fixed) and still attract each other, so the liquid holds a volume but not a shape.
Working: B and D describe solids. A and C together explain liquids.
tips: Solid = fixed positions. Liquid = close but sliding.

explanation_steps: That is why solids keep shape.

options.C: neither fixed shape nor fixed volume

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – Chemistry: The Study of Matter

questions.stem: All atoms of the same element have the same
explanation_steps: Rule: Z (protons) defines the element; chemical properties follow Z. Neutrons and mass number can differ (isotopes).
tips: Isotopes share Z, not A.

similar_questions.stem: Isotopes of an element have the same

options.B: electrons in a neutral atom only

questions.stem: Which of the following diatomic molecules is formed by sharing two pairs of electrons?
explanation_steps: Given: double bond = two shared pairs.
Rule: O₂ is O=O. Cl₂, H₂, F₂ are single; N₂ is triple.
tips: Count shared pairs: single 1, double 2, triple 3.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – Chemical Symbols, Formulas and Equations

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect?

options.A: The nucleus of an atom is positively charged.
options.B: The nucleus of an atom occupies an extremely large volume of space.
options.C: The atomic mass of an atom is determined by the number of protons and neutrons.
options.D: The atom of an element exhibits all the characteristic properties of the element.

explanation_steps: Rule: the nucleus is tiny, not a large volume.
tips: Almost all mass is in a very small nucleus.

similar_questions.stem: Most of the volume of an atom is

questions.stem: Which of the following species are capable of forming hydrogen bonding among themselves?
explanation_steps: Rule: H must be bonded to F, O or N. Only H₂O qualifies.
tips: H-bond partners: FON only.

similar_questions.stem: The strongest intermolecular force in water is

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect?

options.A: A covalent bond can exist between a metal and a non-metal.
options.B: Atoms combine in order to attain a stable noble gas configuration.
options.D: Sharing of electrons forms covalent bond.

explanation_steps: Rule: Eritrean Grade 9/10 treat metal + non-metal as ionic, not covalent.
Working: B, C and D are standard true statements.
tips: Metal + non-metal → ionic in this course.
questions.review_flag: Option A is the intended false line in the local textbook; some compounds (e.g. AlCl₃) are polar covalent.

questions.stem: A certain amount of gas at 1.2 atm and at 35°C has a volume of 120 mL. The gas is heated to 70°C at the same pressure. What would be its volume? (R=0.082 atm·L/mol·K)
explanation_steps: Given: V₁=120 mL, T₁=308 K, T₂=343 K, P constant.
Working: V₂=120×343/308=133.6 mL. R is unused.
tips: Same P → use Kelvin temperatures.

similar_questions.stem: 100 mL of gas at 27°C becomes what at 127°C, P fixed?

questions.stem: In which of the following does a coordinate covalent bond exist?
explanation_steps: Rule: one atom donates both electrons of the pair. SO₂ is the usual Grade 10 example.
tips: Look for an atom that still needs an octet after a double bond — S in SO₂.

explanation_steps: N donates a pair to H⁺.

questions.stem: The molecular formula of the compound with an empirical formula CH₃ and molar mass of 30 g/mol is
explanation_steps: Given: EF = CH₃ (15 g/mol), MF mass = 30.
tips: Molecular = n × empirical.

questions.stem: An atom with the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² is not most likely to be:

options.A: A metal that forms a positive ion.
options.B: A non-metal that forms a negative ion.

explanation_steps: Rule: it is a metal that forms Ca²⁺, not a non-metal anion.
tips: 4s² after argon = alkaline-earth metal.

questions.stem: Which of the following has a trigonal pyramidal molecular geometry?
explanation_steps: Rule: NH₃ is AX₃E, trigonal pyramidal. H₂O bent, BF₃ trigonal planar, CH₄ tetrahedral.
tips: Count bonded atoms and lone pairs.

questions.stem: A crystal system has a unit cell with edges of length a=b≠c, angles between edges α=β=90°, and γ=120° is known as _________
explanation_steps: Rule: that is the hexagonal unit cell.
tips: Hexagonal: two equal sides and a 120° angle.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 Grade 12 – Shapes of Molecules and Crystals

questions.stem: A solid is hard, brittle, and electrically non-conducting. Its molten state and an aqueous solution containing the substance conduct electricity. Classify the solid as
explanation_steps: Given: hard, brittle, insulator as solid; conducts when molten or in water.
Rule: free ions only when melted or dissolved → ionic crystal.
tips: Ionic: conducts only when ions can move.

questions.stem: Which of the following contains the largest number of moles? (At. Mass N=14, H=1, O=16, C=12)
explanation_steps: Rule: n = m/M. Smallest M gives largest n.
Working: NH₃=17, H₂O=18, N₂=28, O₂=32, CO₂=44. Largest n is NH₃.
tips: Same mass: lightest formula wins.

similar_questions.stem: Which 1 g sample has most molecules?

questions.stem: Predict the chemical formula formed from Aluminium and Sulphur. (A. No. Al=13, S=16)
tips: Swap the charges to get the formula.

questions.stem: Which of the following pair of elements can form a highly ionic bond?
explanation_steps: Rule: biggest electronegativity gap is Cs (lowest) and F (highest).
Working: NaCl is ionic but less so than CsF.
tips: Far-left metal + fluorine = most ionic.

similar_questions.stem: The most covalent of these is

questions.stem: The percentage composition of nitrogen in urea (CO(NH₂)₂) is (At. mass C=12, O=16, N=14, H=1)
tips: Two N atoms, not one.

questions.stem: How many moles of CO₂ molecules will be produced, if 2 moles of methane gas react with excess oxygen gas? CH₄ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + heat
explanation_steps: Rule: balanced: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O, so CH₄:CO₂ = 1:1.
tips: Carbon atoms are conserved one-for-one.

similar_questions.stem: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Moles of water from 4 mol H₂?

questions.stem: A student measures 10.0 g of hydrated sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃ · xH₂O) and places it in a crucible. After heating, 3.7 g of anhydrous sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) remains. What is the formula for the hydrate? (At. Wts: Na=23, C=12, O=16, H=1)
explanation_steps: Given: 10.0 g hydrate → 3.7 g Na₂CO₃ so 6.3 g water lost.
tips: Water lost ÷ 18, anhydrous ÷ 106, then divide.

similar_questions.stem: 5 g hydrate loses 1.8 g water and leaves 3.2 g salt of M=160. x is about

questions.stem: Which of these is the chemical formula for sulfurous acid?
explanation_steps: Rule: –ous acid of sulfate family is H₂SO₃; sulfuric is H₂SO₄.
tips: –ous → fewer oxygens than –ic.

questions.stem: Which of the following has the largest ionic radius? (At. No. Na=11, Cl=17, S=16, F=9, O=8)
explanation_steps: Rule: more shells → larger; for same shell, more negative charge → larger. S²⁻ and Cl⁻ are Period 3; S²⁻ is larger than Cl⁻.
tips: Anions bigger than parent; extra charge expands S²⁻.

questions.stem: 2 moles of Hydrogen molecule is not the same as:
explanation_steps: Rule: 2 mol H₂ = 4 g = 44.8 L STP = 2×6.02×10²³ molecules = 4 mol of H atoms, not 4 atoms.
tips: Mole-scale numbers, not four atoms.

questions.stem: Which of the following is false about the modern periodic table?

options.A: Elements that are found in the same period have the same number of shells.
options.B: Elements having the same number of valence electrons show similar chemical properties.
options.C: Elements that are found in the same group have the same valence electrons.
options.D: The elements in the modern periodic table are periodic function of their atomic numbers.

explanation_steps: Rule: A–D are all standard true statements of the modern table.
tips: Period = shells; group = valence electrons.

questions.stem: The common name of elements in group IIA in the periodic table is the:
tips: IA alkali, IIA alkaline earth, VIIA halogen, 0 noble gas.

questions.stem: A compound in which a more reactive element displaces the less active one from its compound is known as
explanation_steps: Given: more reactive replaces less reactive.
Rule: that is a single / simple displacement.
tips: One element in, one element out.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a decomposition reaction?
explanation_steps: Given: find one reactant → two products.
tips: Decomposition: one compound breaks up.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true about an exothermic reaction?

options.D: Heat is absorbed from the surrounding

explanation_steps: Rule: heat is released, so H_products < H_reactants and ∆H is negative.
tips: Exo = heat out = negative ∆H.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 5 Grade 10 – Energy and Chemical Reactions

questions.stem: Tritium is the isotope of ________________.
explanation_steps: Rule: hydrogen isotopes are protium, deuterium, tritium (³H).
tips: Tritium = ³H, two neutrons.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes is/are endothermic?
explanation_steps: Rule: limestone decomposition and boiling both take in heat. Combustion and condensation release heat.
tips: Breaking bonds / vaporising needs heat.

questions.stem: Which of the following reactions has the slowest rate?
explanation_steps: Rule: rusting is the textbook very-slow reaction; neutralisation and chain reactions are fast.
tips: Rusting takes days to years.

similar_questions.stem: The fastest of these is usually

questions.review_flag: Photosynthesis is also slow; the intended school-book example of a very slow reaction is rusting.

questions.stem: The rate of the following chemical reaction can be increased by the following except: CaCO₃(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g)
explanation_steps: Rule: larger pieces lower surface area and slow the reaction. Powder, heat and concentration speed it.
tips: Bigger lumps = slower. Powder = faster.

questions.stem: The catalyst used in the manufacture of Nitric acid (Ostwald’s process) is:
explanation_steps: Rule: NH₃ is oxidised on a hot platinum catalyst. Fe is Haber; V₂O₅ is Contact.
tips: Ostwald = Pt. Haber = Fe. Contact = V₂O₅.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 Grade 11 – Chemistry of Some Nonmetals

questions.stem: Consider the following reaction; NH₃ + H₂O ↔ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ : In the reaction water acts as
explanation_steps: Given: water donates H⁺ to NH₃.
Rule: Brønsted acid = proton donor. Water is the acid here; NH₃ is the base.
Working: amphoteric is a general property of water, but in THIS reaction it acts as an acid.
tips: Follow the proton: water lost H⁺.

questions.stem: The selective passage of solvent molecules through a porous membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one is known as:
explanation_steps: Given: solvent through a membrane, dilute → concentrated.
tips: Osmosis = solvent only, through a membrane.

options.A: spreading of particles down a gradient

questions.stem: 10 grams of a solid substance is placed in 100 grams of water at 20°C and the entire solid dissolved. Then another 6 grams of the same substance is added at 20°C and one third of it dissolved. Which of the following is true about the first solution?
explanation_steps: Given: first 10 g all dissolved; later 2 g more still dissolved.
Rule: the first solution could still take more solute, so it was unsaturated.
tips: If more solid can dissolve, it was unsaturated.

options.A: can dissolve no more solute at that T

questions.stem: Compared to Rainwater, Seawater will have a _____________ vapor pressure.
explanation_steps: Rule: a non-volatile solute lowers vapour pressure.
tips: More particles in seawater → lower VP.

questions.stem: What is the molarity of a solution which contains 0.05 mol of H₂SO₄ in 250 mL of solution?
tips: Change mL to litres first.

questions.stem: Physical properties of solutions that are affected by the number of particles but not on the identity of the dissolved solute particles are called ___________.
explanation_steps: Given: depend on count, not identity.
tips: BP up, FP down, VP down, osmotic pressure.

questions.stem: In diluting solutions,

options.A: The final volume is greater than the initial volume
options.B: The amount of solute is changed
options.C: The final concentration is less than the initial concentration
options.D: The number of moles is changed

explanation_steps: Rule: add solvent only. Moles of solute stay the same; volume up, concentration down.
tips: M₁V₁ = M₂V₂. Solute moles fixed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most unstable type of solution?
explanation_steps: Rule: supersaturated holds extra solute and crystallises easily.
tips: A seed crystal drops a supersaturated solution.

questions.stem: Which of the following yields two hydrogen ions upon complete ionization?
explanation_steps: Rule: a diprotic acid. H₂CO₃ → 2H⁺ + CO₃²⁻ (complete). HCl and acetic are monoprotic; H₃PO₄ is triprotic.
tips: Count replaceable hydrogens.
questions.review_flag: Printed options were jumbled (H₃PO₄ and HNO appeared twice). Reconstructed as A acetic, B carbonic, C phosphoric, D hydrochloric.

questions.stem: One of the following is not the property of a bases?

options.B: It turns red litmus paper to blue.
options.C: It produces hydrogen ions when dissolved in water.

explanation_steps: Rule: bases produce OH⁻, not H⁺. H⁺ is the acid ion.
tips: Acid: H⁺ / sour / blue→red. Base: OH⁻ / bitter / red→blue.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an application of a neutralization reaction?
explanation_steps: Rule: lime on soil, toothpaste and antacids are neutralization. Making acids is manufacture, not neutralization.
tips: Neutralisation treats extra acid or extra base.

questions.stem: Identify the basic oxide from the following compounds?
explanation_steps: Rule: Group I metal oxide K₂O is basic. CO₂, SO₃, NO are acidic; Al₂O₃ is amphoteric.
tips: Metal oxides (except amphoteric ones) are basic.

questions.stem: Which of the following salts is insoluble in water?
explanation_steps: Rule: most sulfates dissolve; BaSO₄ is the classic exception. Group I and ammonium salts dissolve.
tips: Remember BaSO₄ / PbSO₄ as insoluble sulfates.

questions.stem: If the pOH of an aqueous solution is 3, then the solution is said to be
explanation_steps: Rule: pH + pOH = 14, so pH = 11, which is basic.
tips: pOH < 7 means basic.

questions.stem: What is the boiling point of an aqueous solution if its boiling point elevation is 0.01°C
tips: Elevation means above 100°C.

questions.stem: During electrolysis;

options.A: Reduction takes place at the cathode
options.C: Both oxidation and reduction takes place at the anode.
options.E: Oxidation takes place at the cathode.

explanation_steps: Rule: cathode is negative → cations reduced there. Anode is oxidation.
tips: RED CAT: reduction at cathode.

similar_questions.stem: Oxidation in a cell happens at the

questions.stem: The oxidation number of Chlorine in KClO₃ is:
tips: Chlorate is Cl +5; perchlorate is +7.

similar_questions.stem: Oxidation number of Cl in NaCl is

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of weak electrolyte in its aqueous solution?
explanation_steps: Rule: weak acid H₂CO₃ ionises only partly. The others are strong.
tips: Weak acid / weak base = weak electrolyte.

questions.stem: Which of the following is found in uncombined state?
explanation_steps: Rule: unreactive gold occurs native. Na, Ca are too reactive; Fe and Pb are usually combined.
tips: Low in the reactivity series → found free.

questions.stem: Metalloids;

options.A: Have property of non metal only
options.B: have conductivity that depends on temperature.

explanation_steps: Rule: they are semiconductors — conductivity rises with temperature.
tips: Si and Ge sit on the metal/non-metal line.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true in case of an ideal gas?

options.B: It obeys gas laws under all conditions of temperature and pressure.
options.C: There are no intermolecular forces of attraction between molecules.
options.D: The volume occupied by molecules is negligible.

explanation_steps: Rule: real gases are not always ideal and do not obey the laws at all T and P. C and D are the ideal-gas assumptions.
tips: Ideal gas = point masses, no attractions, laws at low P high T.

similar_questions.stem: Real gases behave most ideally at

questions.stem: Which of the following relationships of gases is stated by Boyle’s Law?

options.B: V ∝ n (at constant P and T)
options.C: V ∝ T (at constant n and P)
options.D: P ∝ T (at constant n and V)
options.E: V ∝ P (at constant n and T)

explanation_steps: Rule: P V = constant at fixed T and n, so V ∝ 1/P.
tips: Boyle = inverse P and V. Charles = V ∝ T.

questions.stem: A given mass of a certain gas occupies a volume of 30 cm³ at 300 K. What volume will it occupy if the temperature is raised to 320 K, while keeping the pressure constant?
explanation_steps: Given: V₁=30 cm³, T₁=300 K, T₂=320 K.
tips: Charles: volume follows Kelvin T.

similar_questions.stem: 60 cm³ at 200 K becomes what at 300 K, P fixed?

questions.stem: The chemical symbols for Cobalt, Potassium, & Calcium are respectively:
explanation_steps: Rule: Co, K, Ca. P is phosphorus; CO is carbon monoxide.
tips: Two-letter symbols: only the first letter is capital.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an organic compound?
explanation_steps: Rule: CH₃OH (methanol) is a carbon hydride/alcohol. The others are inorganic salts or carbide.
tips: Organic here means C covalently bound to H (and O).

questions.stem: The molecule which contains an ester functional group is:
explanation_steps: Rule: R–COO–R′ is an ester. A aldehyde, B ketone, D ether, E carboxylic acid.
tips: Ester = acid + alcohol, look for –COO– between carbons.

questions.stem: All the members of the homologous series
explanation_steps: Rule: same general formula and functional group, similar chemistry, physical properties that change gradually (so they differ).
tips: Each member adds CH₂.

questions.stem: What is the general formula for the following homologous series of hydrocarbon? (C₂H₂, C₃H₄, C₄H₆)
tips: Alkane 2n+2, alkene 2n, alkyne 2n−2.

questions.stem: Which of the following gases is prepared by treating calcium carbide with water?
tips: Carbide lamp gas is acetylene.

similar_questions.stem: Methane is made in the lab from

questions.stem: How many moles of oxygen gas are exactly required for the complete combustion of one mole of butane?
explanation_steps: Rule: 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O, so 6.5 mol O₂ per mol butane.
tips: General: CₓHᵧ + (x + y/4)O₂.

similar_questions.stem: Complete combustion of 1 mol CH₄ needs

questions.stem: The process of soap formation by alkaline hydrolysis of fats or oils is known as:
tips: Soap = sodium/potassium salt of a long-chain acid.

options.A: an ionic head and a hydrocarbon tail

questions.stem: The process by which large and less volatile hydrocarbons are broken down into a variety of smaller and more volatile ones is known as
explanation_steps: Rule: cracking. Distillation only separates; it does not break chains.
tips: Cracking makes petrol and ethene from heavy oil.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a secondary alcohol?
explanation_steps: Rule: secondary = C–OH attached to two carbons. 2-butanol is CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃. A is primary; C and D are tertiary.
tips: Look at how many C atoms sit on the C–OH carbon.

questions.stem: Which one of the following polymers is formed by condensation polymerisation?
explanation_steps: Rule: polyester is made by condensation (ester links + water). The others are addition polymers of alkenes.
tips: Condensation polymers: polyester, nylon, protein.

questions.stem: The radioactive emission which emits the heaviest particle in the form of radiation is
explanation_steps: Rule: α is a ⁴He nucleus (mass 4). β and positron are electrons; γ has no mass.
tips: Alpha = heaviest and least penetrating.

questions.stem: ____________ is the splitting of a heavy nucleus into smaller more stable fragments.
explanation_steps: Rule: fission. Fusion joins light nuclei.
tips: Fission = split. Fusion = join.

questions.stem: A half-life period of a radioactive element is 1.5 years. What amount of it will be left after 4.5 year if you start with 16 grams of it?
explanation_steps: Given: t½=1.5 y, t=4.5 y, m₀=16 g.
tips: After n half-lives, mass is m₀/2ⁿ.

similar_questions.stem: 8 g with t½=2 days after 6 days is

questions.stem: ²⁷₁₃Al can be prepared by beta emission from
explanation_steps: Given: product ²⁷₁₃Al by β⁻ emission.
Rule: β⁻ raises Z by 1 and keeps A. Parent is ²⁷₁₂Mg.
tips: β⁻: neutron → proton, Z increases by 1.

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect about nuclear reactions?

options.A: Temperature has no effect on the rate of nuclear reactions.
options.C: Elements (isotopes) are converted from one to another.
options.D: These reactions are irreversible in nature.

explanation_steps: Given: find a false textbook line.
Rule: A–D are the usual Grade 12 statements comparing nuclear and chemical change. None is treated as false.
tips: Nuclear rates do not follow ordinary T-dependence.

similar_questions.stem: Energy per gram is larger in

questions.stem: What are the factors that affect the rate of a chemical reaction? List four.
questions.answer: Temperature; concentration (or pressure for gases); surface area / particle size; catalyst (also nature of reactants).
accepted_answers: Temperature; concentration (or pressure for gases); surface area / particle size; catalyst (also nature of reactants).
explanation_steps: Rule: collision theory — more / better collisions raise rate.
Answer: temperature, concentration, surface area, catalyst.
questions.marking_points: 0.5 each for any four of: temperature; concentration; pressure (gases); surface area/particle size; catalyst; nature of reactants; light (for photochemical).
tips: Name a factor then say how it changes collisions.

similar_questions.stem: Name two ways to speed CaCO₃ + HCl.
similar_questions.answer: Powder the CaCO₃; warm the acid / use more concentrated HCl.

questions.stem: Commercial HCl is 36% by mass of hydrogen chloride and has a density of 1.18 g/mL. Determine the molarity of the solution. (M. mass of HCl = 36.5 g/mol).
explanation_steps: Rule: mass HCl in 1.00 L = 0.36 × 1180 g = 424.8 g.
questions.marking_points: 1 for mass of 1 L; 1 for mass of HCl; 1 for moles and molarity.
tips: M = (10 × % × density) / molar mass, with d in g/mL.

similar_questions.stem: A 40% w/w NaOH solution has density 1.4 g/mL. Molarity? (M=40)

questions.stem: The solubility of CuSO₄ at 85°C is 60 g and at 15°C is 18.8 g (per 100 g water). If 120 g of water saturated at 85°C were cooled to 15°C, what mass of CuSO₄ would be precipitated?
explanation_steps: Given: 60 g/100 g at 85°C; 18.8 g/100 g at 15°C; 120 g water.
Working: dissolved at 85°C = 60×1.20=72.0 g. Remaining at 15°C = 18.8×1.20=22.56 g.
questions.marking_points: 1 for scale to 120 g water; 1 for 72 g; 1 for 22.56 g; 1 for difference.
tips: Solubility figures are usually per 100 g water — scale first.

similar_questions.stem: Solubility 50 g/100 g at 80°C and 20 g/100 g at 20°C. 50 g water cooled. Mass precipitated?

questions.stem:
A) Classify each of the following aliphatic hydrocarbons as saturated or unsaturated. (2 pts) I. 2-Butene  II. 2-methyl propane
B) Complete the following reactions and give the correct IUPAC name for each product and reactant. (4 pts)
I. CH₃–CH₂–OH  (conc. H₂SO₄, heat) → ________
II. CH₂=CH₂ + Cl₂ → ________
questions.answer: A-I unsaturated (2-butene); A-II saturated (2-methylpropane). B-I ethanol → ethene + water. B-II ethene → 1,2-dichloroethane.
accepted_answers: A-I unsaturated (2-butene); A-II saturated (2-methylpropane). B-I ethanol → ethene + water. B-II ethene → 1,2-dichloroethane.
explanation_steps: Rule: C=C is unsaturated; only single C–C is saturated. Conc. H₂SO₄ dehydrates ethanol; Cl₂ adds to ethene.
Answer: A-I unsaturated; A-II saturated; B-I ethene; B-II 1,2-dichloroethane.
questions.marking_points: 1 each for A-I and A-II. 1 for each correct product formula/name in B (4).
tips: Alkene names end in –ene; addition to C=C is typical.

questions.stem:
A. Complete the nuclear equation: ²⁶₁₂Mg + ¹₁P → ⁴₂α + ________ (1 pt)
B. Complete and name reactants and products: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–COOH + Na → ________ (2 pts)
questions.answer: A. ²³₁₁Na. B. CH₃(CH₂)₃COONa + ½H₂ (sodium pentanoate / sodium pentanoate and hydrogen).
accepted_answers: A. ²³₁₁Na. B. CH₃(CH₂)₃COONa + ½H₂ (sodium pentanoate / sodium pentanoate and hydrogen).
explanation_steps: Given: capture a proton and lose alpha; carboxylic acid + Na.
Working A: mass 26+1−4=23; atomic number 12+1−2=11 → ²³₁₁Na.
Working B: acid + metal → salt + hydrogen. Pentanoic acid → sodium pentanoate.
questions.marking_points: 1 for the nuclide. 1 for the salt formula/name; 1 for hydrogen.
tips: Balance A and Z separately in nuclear equations.

questions.stem: Write a balanced chemical equation for each of the following reactions when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with: a. Zinc metal. b. Potassium hydroxide. c. Which of the above reactions produces a gas?
questions.answer: a. Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. b. KOH + HCl → KCl + H₂O. c. The zinc reaction produces hydrogen gas.
accepted_answers: a. Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. b. KOH + HCl → KCl + H₂O. c. The zinc reaction produces hydrogen gas.
explanation_steps: Given: dilute HCl with metal and with alkali.
Rule: metal + acid → salt + H₂; acid + base → salt + water.
Answer: a H₂; b water; c the zinc reaction.
questions.marking_points: 1 for each balanced equation; 1 for identifying the gas-producing reaction.
tips: Active metal + acid always gives hydrogen.

questions.stem: A 25 mL of a 0.020 M nitric acid solution is titrated with 0.01 M potassium hydroxide solution. a) What is the pH at the equivalence point? b) What is the volume of the base needed to reach the equivalence point?
questions.answer: a) pH = 7. b) 50 mL of KOH.
accepted_answers: a) pH = 7. b) 50 mL of KOH.
explanation_steps: Given: 25 mL of 0.020 M HNO₃ vs 0.010 M KOH.
Rule: strong acid + strong base → salt water, pH 7. n(acid)=0.025×0.020=5.0×10⁻⁴ mol. V(base)=n/C=0.050 L=50 mL.
questions.marking_points: 2 for pH 7 with reason; 2 for 50 mL working.
tips: Strong–strong titration equivalence is pH 7 at 25°C.
